# Net Forge idle template (BRINEWORKS)

> A shared salt flat for up to 8 players. Each player runs a works on a
> plot: pumps draw brine, pans boil it into salt, kilns cut salt into
> crystals, and salt buys and levels more plants. Players rake by hand for
> salt, and everyone ships crystals to one contract barge. A shift has a
> fixed length; then a new shift starts from nothing.
> You change the game by editing src/game.ts only. The template already has
> the works, the production chain, buying and levelling, raking, tending,
> the contract, the shift clock, netcode, rendering, earn and the store.

## Files

- src/game.ts: THE GAME. game(), saltFlat(), plant(), upgrade(),
  earn.rule(), earn.stake(), store.sku().
- src/names.json: the title and every label. Plants go in "weapons"
  ({ name, line }); "enemies" stays empty.

## Rules the build enforces (the anti-farm rules)

- game({ template: "idle", style, places, players: { prefab, max } }), max at most 8.
- Exactly one saltFlat(...); 1 to 8 plant(...)s with at least one "pump",
  one "pan" and one "kiln" (the chain).
- A shift is 600 to 3600 seconds. Every earn rule is oncePer: "run" (a run
  is a shift, or a player's time in it).
- tend is at most 300 seconds: a works nobody tends stops, so an idle tab
  makes nothing. Production happens only on the room's clock while the
  player is in the room; nothing is earned offline and a player who leaves
  and comes back starts a fresh works.
- No earn rule may pay sooner than 180 seconds into a fresh works, even
  with perfect play or raking as fast as the cooldown allows. The gate
  measures it; if a draft pays sooner it fails with the number. Raise
  packEvery or the rule's n, or slow raking.
- Upgrades read three stats: might (plant output), haste (raking speed),
  amount (salt a rake). No weapon() or prefab().
- An earn rule must fire within about 4 minutes of 4-player play.

## Units

Seconds, litres of brine, kg of salt, whole crystals. A plant's rate is a
second, a level. Costs are kg of salt; each level costs growth times the last.

## Common changes

### Faster or slower progress
plant("hand_pump", { model: "style.lowpoly.barrel", kind: "pump", cost: 15, growth: 1.15, rate: 3 });
Lower growth makes levels cheap for longer; a higher rate makes each level count more.
Keep the first payout at least 180 s away (the gate checks).

### A new plant
plant("deep_bore", { model: "style.lowpoly.generator_large", kind: "pump", cost: 5000, growth: 1.2, rate: 200 });
Add its label to names.json weapons. The bar shows plants in order (keys 1-8).

### Longer or shorter shifts
saltFlat({ shift: 1200, ... }) (600 to 3600 s). A bigger contract: contract: { crystals: 120 }.

### Earn rules
earn.rule("first_crate", { when: "salt.packed", n: 30, pay: 5, oncePer: "run" });
Events: salt.packed (one each packEvery kg a player makes), crystal.cut,
crystal.shipped, plant.built, plant.upgraded (each credits the player),
contract.filled (the players who shipped to it; world progress, so never a
player whose run started after the shift began). Pays coins once a run.

### The buy-in run (required)
earn.stake({ min: 20, max: 200, multiple: 2 }); one top-level line. "stake" is reserved.

### Coins: earn and the store
store.sku("bellows", { coins: 40 });                               // one level of "bellows" for the shift
store.sku("skin_rust", { coins: 500, grants: { cosmetic: 2 } });   // a finish for your foreman
store.sku("brass_bellows", { coins: 150, grants: { gear: "bellows", loseBelow: 0.25 } }); // losable gear
Keep the SKUs the client is wired to (bellows, long_rake, quick_hands,
skin_saltwhite, skin_rust, brass_bellows) at their prices.

## Test

engine.test.run({ ticks: 30 * 240, bots: 4 }) plays the flat and reports
crates packed (as kills), earned by rule, softlock, ms per tick and the
genre's checks (the farming bounds) under rules.checks.

## Worked example: src/game.ts

This is the template's complete src/game.ts as it ships. A new game on this
template starts from this file and changes declarations in place.

```ts
/**
 * BRINEWORKS: the idle template (play style: idle).
 *
 * A white salt flat under a hot sky. Up to eight players each run a works on
 * the flat: pumps draw brine, pans boil it into salt, kilns cut salt into
 * crystals, and salt buys and levels more plants. A barge on the canal
 * takes crystals for a contract everyone fills together. A shift lasts
 * fifteen minutes; then the flat is raked clean and a new shift begins.
 *
 * Works run only while their player is on the flat and has tended them in
 * the last two minutes (a rake, a purchase, a shipment): no offline
 * production, nothing for an idle tab.
 *
 * This file is the whole game as the model writes it: declarations only,
 * against the typed API in @netforge/engine.
 */
import { earn, game, plant, saltFlat, store, upgrade } from "@netforge/engine";

export default game({
  template: "idle",
  style: "lowpoly",
  places: { flat: { chunks: "places/flat", spawn: [0, 0, 0] } },
  players: { prefab: "style.lowpoly.worker", max: 8 },
});

// The flat: a fifteen-minute shift, works that stall two minutes after the last tend,
// a rake every 0.4 s for 3 kg, 3 L of brine to a kg of salt, 25 kg of salt to a crystal, a crate every 150 kg.
saltFlat({
  shift: 900,
  tend: 120,
  start: 20,
  rake: { salt: 3, cooldown: 0.4 },
  brinePerSalt: 3,
  saltPerCrystal: 25,
  packEvery: 150,
  contract: { crystals: 60 },
});

// Plants. cost is kg of salt for the first level, growth the price rise a level; rate is a second, a level
// (pumps: litres of brine; pans: kg of salt boiled; kilns: crystals cut).
plant("hand_pump", { model: "style.lowpoly.barrel", kind: "pump", cost: 15, growth: 1.15, rate: 3 });
plant("boil_pan", { model: "style.lowpoly.crate", kind: "pan", cost: 25, growth: 1.15, rate: 1 });
plant("steam_pump", { model: "style.lowpoly.generator", kind: "pump", cost: 400, growth: 1.18, rate: 30 });
plant("sun_pan", { model: "style.lowpoly.barrels", kind: "pan", cost: 600, growth: 1.18, rate: 10 });
plant("crystal_kiln", { model: "style.lowpoly.generator_large", kind: "kiln", cost: 900, growth: 1.25, rate: 0.05 });

// Store upgrades: one level each, for the rest of the shift, on the buyer's own works.
upgrade("bellows", { stat: "might", step: 0.15, maxLevel: 1 });
upgrade("long_rake", { stat: "amount", step: 0.3, maxLevel: 1 });
upgrade("quick_hands", { stat: "haste", step: 0.25, maxLevel: 1 });

// Earn (mandatory). Pays the game's coins (1 coin = 1 token), once a shift each. Values are PLACEHOLDER.
earn.rule("first_crate", { when: "salt.packed", n: 30, pay: 5, oncePer: "run" });
earn.rule("long_haul", { when: "salt.packed", n: 300, pay: 20, oncePer: "run" });
earn.rule("full_hold", { when: "contract.filled", n: 1, pay: 50, oncePer: "run" });
earn.rule("cutter", { when: "crystal.cut", n: 30, pay: 5, oncePer: "run" });
// Buy-in run (the mandatory sink loop): stake coins at shift start to earn above free play. Values are PLACEHOLDER.
earn.stake({ min: 20, max: 200, multiple: 2 });

// Store (the Kit), priced in coins: three shift upgrades, two finishes owned for good, one piece of losable gear.
store.sku("bellows", { coins: 40 });
store.sku("long_rake", { coins: 40 });
store.sku("quick_hands", { coins: 60 });
store.sku("skin_saltwhite", { coins: 300, grants: { cosmetic: 1 } });
store.sku("skin_rust", { coins: 500, grants: { cosmetic: 2 } });
// Losable gear: owned for good until lost. It brings one level of its upgrade into every staked shift,
// and is lost when that shift makes less than loseBelow of its most earn. Values are PLACEHOLDER.
store.sku("brass_bellows", { coins: 150, grants: { gear: "bellows", loseBelow: 0.25 } });
```

## Validate and playtest

### With the MCP server

Run `npx -y @netforge/mcp` (package @netforge/mcp, bin netforge-mcp) and
connect it to your coding agent. Its tools are netforge_list_templates, netforge_create_game,
netforge_explain_api, netforge_search_docs, netforge_validate_game, netforge_run_playtest and netforge_play_locally.

- netforge_validate_game checks src/game.ts against the engine's schemas and this
  template's rules, and returns one actionable line per problem.
- netforge_run_playtest plays the game headless with bots and returns the report.
- netforge_play_locally gives the steps to open the game in a browser with kit play.

### In code

Import the game module first so its declarations register, then run the
headless harness. This plays 4 players for 4 minutes at 30 Hz.

```ts
import { engine } from "@netforge/engine";
import "./src/game.js";

const report = await engine.test.run({
  ticks: 30 * 240,
  bots: 4,
  seed: 1,
  assert: [
    { name: "earn fired", check: (r) => r.earnEmitted > 0 },
    { name: "no softlock", check: (r) => !r.softlock },
  ],
});
if (report.failed.length > 0) throw new Error(report.failed.join("\n"));
```

The report has crates packed (as kills), earned by rule, softlock, ms per tick and the genre's checks (the farming bounds) under rules.checks.

The template's own tests (vitest) are the reference checks:

- test/harness.test.ts
- test/store.test.ts

### Play it locally

In a folder with netnet.json and src/game.ts:

```sh
npm install @netforge/kit-play @netforge/engine @netforge/template-idle
echo '{"template":"idle"}' > netnet.json
npx kit-play        # opens http://127.0.0.1:4663
```

kit play builds the template client with your src/game.ts and runs a local
room host with play money. No wallet, no chain and no hosted servers are
involved. Open the link in more tabs for more players.
